account: A US criminal and traffic defense law firm

summary.funnel: Lead generation, ad impression to lead (Google Ads Search)
summary.sources: Google Ads for every step; GA4 not connected for this business, so the site steps are taken from the account's own conversion actions
summary.biggest_leak: Criminal Defense campaign: 27.3% impression share (35.5% in the comparison window; under the 30% 'low below' floor, so at least high), up to 93 leads a month as a ceiling
summary.likely_cause: Budget runs out on the two cheapest non-brand campaigns, so the top of the funnel shrank while the click-to-lead rate held.
summary.first_fix: Check that the 'Call or Text' action counts real conversations, then move budget from Drug Charges into Criminal Defense and Traffic Tickets.

trust_checks.detail: 5 enabled conversion actions are counted; they recorded 185 leads in the window.
Conversion value is 0 on every campaign, and no qualified-lead or signed-case step is imported. The funnel ends at leads, and impact is counted in leads and spend.

'Call or Text (website)' is a counted website action and recorded 64 of the 185 leads (34.6%). Its name and type suggest a tap on a call or text button, not a completed call or message. If so, the lead step is inflated by up to that share.

The contact-page load action recorded 9 visits, but the contact form recorded 46 leads. Forms are submitted on landing pages without a visit to the contact page, so the page load is not a step before the form and is left out of the funnel.
GA4 is not connected for this business; the ad platform records impressions and clicks itself.
Needs GA4 Paid Search sessions to compare with the clicks; GA4 is not connected for this business.

funnel_map.source: GA4 is not connected for this business

lead_routes_note: Calls from ads happen on the results page and never reach the site; the other routes start with a site visit.
score_working: 100 - 10 x 1 high - 20 x 1 critical - 4 x 0 moderate = 70
segment_notes: Each rate has one reference that sets its severity: a campaign's impression share and click rate against its own comparison window; click-to-lead against the other non-brand campaigns (Brand against its own window), devices against the other devices and landing pages against the other pages. The other comparison is shown as context only.
The 'low below' lines (30% impression share, 2% click rate, 4% click to lead) are floors for the account totals and every non-brand segment, with or without history; Brand is exempt.
Campaigns or pages with under 30 clicks are listed but not graded.

38 other regions each sent under 30 clicks, so they are added together and never graded one by one. Every click from them came from the two out-of-state campaigns, which target other states on purpose, and every other campaign's clicks came from the home state, so here the region split repeats the campaign split.
The free case evaluation page turned 10 of 18 ad clicks into leads: too few to grade, but a candidate page to test against the weak drug-charges page.
Leads from the landing-page report (115) are fewer than the account's 185, because calls from ads have no landing page.

leaks.reference: 35.5% in the comparison window; under the 30% 'low below' floor, so at least high
leaks.counted_part_note: Lost 41.4% to budget and 31.4% to rank. Both parts count (leads cost $19, at or under the account's $30); the budget part costs more leads, so it sets the impact.
Lost 26.9% to budget and 20.3% to rank. Both parts count (leads cost $24, at or under the account's $30); the budget part costs more leads, so it sets the impact.
Lost 10.2% to rank and none to budget, so the rank part sets the impact.
Lost 19.4% to budget and 1.4% to rank. The budget part is not counted, because leads here cost $131 against the account's $30; only the rank part counts, although budget was the bigger loss.

do first: #1 Leads: Confirm what 'Call or Text (website)' records

#2 Below leads: Import the step after the lead: qualified consultations or signed cases from the intake system as an offline conversion, with a value per case, so the funnel reaches revenue and leaks can be priced
#3 Criminal Defense campaign: Move budget from the Drug Charges campaign (the most expensive leads) into this campaign, then raise it in steps while its cost per lead stays under the account's
#4 Traffic Tickets campaign: Move budget from the Drug Charges campaign (the most expensive leads) into this campaign, then raise it in steps while its cost per lead stays under the account's

#5 Drug Charges campaign: Rebuild the drug-charges page above the fold for mobile: the charge-specific headline from the ad, a click-to-call button and a 3-field case review form, plus two case results
quick wins: #6 Brand campaign: Raise the brand keywords' bids or target impression share so the firm's own name shows on every search, and check the brand ads' quality
later: #7 Nursing Board campaign: Leave its budget as it is

top_fixes.fix: Confirm what 'Call or Text (website)' records. If it is a button tap, move it to a secondary action and count a confirmed call (call tracking with a minimum length) or a delivered text instead.
top_fixes.why: 'Call or Text (website)' is a counted website action and recorded 64 of the 185 leads (34.6%). Its name and type suggest a tap on a call or text button, not a completed call or message. If so, the lead step is inflated by up to that share.

top_fixes.fix: Import the step after the lead: qualified consultations or signed cases from the intake system as an offline conversion, with a value per case, so the funnel reaches revenue and leaks can be priced.
top_fixes.why: Conversion value is 0 on every campaign, and no qualified-lead or signed-case step is imported. The funnel ends at leads, and impact is counted in leads and spend.

top_fixes.reference: 35.5% in the comparison window; under the 30% 'low below' floor, so at least high
top_fixes.impact: up to 93 more leads a month (a ceiling) for up to $1,730 more spend, at a cost per lead of $19 against the account's $30
top_fixes.cause_hypothesis: The daily budget runs out: 7,114 eligible impressions were lost to budget in the window.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 13: lost-to-budget share up on the comparison window.
top_fixes.fix: Move budget from the Drug Charges campaign (the most expensive leads) into this campaign, then raise it in steps while its cost per lead stays under the account's.

top_fixes.impact: up to 27 more leads a month (a ceiling) for up to $650 more spend, at a cost per lead of $24 against the account's $30
top_fixes.cause_hypothesis: The daily budget runs out: 903 eligible impressions were lost to budget in the window.
top_fixes.evidence: Call 13: lost-to-budget share up on the comparison window.
top_fixes.fix: Move budget from the Drug Charges campaign (the most expensive leads) into this campaign, then raise it in steps while its cost per lead stays under the account's.

top_fixes.impact: about 6.8 leads a month lost; $830 spent at $166 a lead against the account's $30, so about $680 a month buys nothing extra
top_fixes.cause_hypothesis: The step after the click, not the ad: the campaign's click rate rose from 5.2% to 8.6%, so the ad draws clicks, but the leads don't follow. Its landing page turns 10.0% of 40 clicks into leads against 19.3% on the other landing pages; on 40 clicks that page gap alone is still within noise. Likely causes: the page doesn't answer the search (the charge, the penalties, the cost), the call button and form sit low on mobile, or there is no proof such as case results.
top_fixes.evidence: Calls 14 and 17; confirm with a session recording or a form-field report, and check the page's mobile speed.
top_fixes.fix: Rebuild the drug-charges page above the fold for mobile: the charge-specific headline from the ad, a click-to-call button and a 3-field case review form, plus two case results. Until it converts, cap the campaign's budget.

more_fixes.impact: up to 2 more leads a month (a ceiling)
more_fixes.cause_hypothesis: Ad rank: 10.2% of brand impressions were lost to rank and none to budget.
more_fixes.fix: Raise the brand keywords' bids or target impression share so the firm's own name shows on every search, and check the brand ads' quality; a competitor bidding on the name is the usual cause of brand share lost to rank.

more_fixes.impact: under 1 more lead a month (a ceiling)
more_fixes.cause_hypothesis: Lost 19.4% to budget and 1.4% to rank. The budget part is not counted, because leads here cost $131 against the account's $30; only the rank part counts, although budget was the bigger loss.
more_fixes.fix: Leave its budget as it is; before adding any, find out why its leads cost so much (its keywords, its ads and its landing page), then raise bids only if the cost per lead comes down.

tests.leak: Criminal Defense campaign impressions lost to budget
tests.hypothesis: If the budget rises in steps for 2 weeks each, leads rise while the cost per lead stays under the account's $30, because 7,114 eligible impressions went unserved.
tests.type: stepped budget test (not a split test)
tests.stop_rule: Stop raising when 2 weeks' cost per lead goes above $30.

tests.leak: Traffic Tickets campaign impressions lost to budget
tests.hypothesis: If the budget rises in steps for 2 weeks each, leads rise while the cost per lead stays under the account's $30, because 903 eligible impressions went unserved.
tests.type: stepped budget test (not a split test)
tests.stop_rule: Stop raising when 2 weeks' cost per lead goes above $30.

tests.hypothesis: If the drug-charges page leads with the charge named in the ad, a click-to-call button and a 3-field case review form above the fold on mobile, its click-to-lead rate rises from 11.4% towards 26.9%, because visitors see their charge and the next step without scrolling.
tests.note: At this volume a split test takes months; run the new page for all traffic for 30 days and compare with this window instead, using the same gap test.

monitoring.metric: Mobile vs desktop gap, clicks → leads
monitoring.note: The gap that would count as real at this window's clicks; past it, check the mobile page first.
